youtube_title: Singapore, Michigan: the lumber town buried under Lake Michigan's dunes
body: The ruins of a town lie buried under the sand dunes of Lake Michigan. Singapore was founded in the 1830s by New York land speculators near Saugatuck, Michigan, who hoped it would rival Chicago or Milwaukee. After the Great Chicago Fire of 1871, its lumber helped rebuild the city. But the forests around it had been clear-cut, and in 1875 the main mill was taken apart and shipped north to St. Ignace. People left, some buildings were moved to Saugatuck, and the sand moved in. Legend says one man refused to leave, climbing in and out through an upstairs window until the sand reached the roof. A state historical marker at Saugatuck City Hall says the site lies beneath the sands near the mouth of the Kalamazoo River. Nothing is visible there today; please read the marker in town. 👻 Comment your town, and it could be next! #Saugatuck #Singapore #Michigan #LakeMichigan #GhostTown #History #LaPorteAfterDark
